title: What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: Fashion owes craftspeople more than romantic visibility: lawful and timely pay, safe conditions, credible credit, worker voice, remedy, preserved knowledge, and limits on extraction—specified for the actual relationship and jurisdiction.
Materials such as silk, glass, and metallic thread make skilled transformation visible while the museum record still names only the house as maker.

01 · NAME — Can the worker choose to be credited?. Build role-level credits with consent: cutter, embroiderer, weaver, dyer, machinist, finisher, presser, sample maker, repairer, and others as locally accurate. Protect people where naming creates risk.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · PAY — What commercial decisions reach the workroom?. Trace price, lead time, revisions, cancellations, overtime, payment schedule, subcontracting, and remedy. Purchasing decisions upstream can shape downstream labor outcomes; verify the actual chain.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · VOICE — Who can refuse, correct, and report harm?. Document worker-representation and grievance routes, anti-retaliation protections, safety escalation, correction of public credits, and who controls the response. A feedback form without remedy is not voice.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · KNOWLEDGE — What does preservation return?. With consent, preserve process narration, terminology, samples, and contributor authority. Do not convert community knowledge into proprietary house content without permission, attribution, benefit, and cultural review.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Choose one object and list only the roles the evidence supports; label every missing contributor unresolved.
Map price, lead time, change orders, overtime, subcontracting, payment, and remedy through the actual production chain.
Ask workers or representatives which credit, anonymity, archive, and correction options are safe and useful.
Route wage, classification, safety, contract, and cross-border issues to qualified labor counsel and local specialists.
